title: Illuminated Manuscripts
objective: After this level you can explain how medieval scribes made illuminated manuscripts.
summary: Monks wrote books by hand on calfskin vellum, then laid on gold leaf and polished it to shine: that is illumination. The Book of Kells, about 800, is the most famous.

cards.headline: Illuminated manuscripts really do light up.
cards.body: Tilt a page from a medieval Gospel book and bits of it flash like a mirror. That's real gold. Every one of these books was written and decorated by hand, one page at a time. So how do you make a book that glows?

cards.headline: Step 1: a page made of skin
cards.body: The finest medieval books weren't written on paper but on vellum, a parchment made from calfskin. Most were made in monasteries. The scribe ruled faint lines across the page to keep the writing straight, then wrote with a sharpened quill or a reed pen. No delete key, so concentrate.

cards.headline: Step 2: gold that shines
cards.body: Then came the gold. Thin sheets of gold or silver leaf were laid onto a sticky ground, then polished to a shine with a smooth stone, or even a dog's tooth. Strictly, only a book decorated with gold or silver counts as illuminated (from Latin illuminare). Today the word covers any decorated manuscript.
cards.callout: Illuminated, strictly: decorated with gold or silver that catches the light.

cards.fact: The Book of Kells was made about 800, by monks, entirely by hand.
cards.context: Columban monks wrote the four Gospels in Latin on 340 vellum leaves. Work probably began on the island of Iona, off Scotland; after a Viking raid in 806, the monks moved to Kells in Ireland. Its famous Chi-Rho page is almost all one word: the Greek letters that begin "Christ", swelling into spirals and knots. Look closely and you'll find cats and mice in the decoration.

mascot.line: Cats and mice on the holiest page. Even monks, it seems, liked a small joke in the margins.

cards.headline: Manuscripts: illuminated
learned: Fine books were written by hand on calfskin vellum
Illuminated strictly means decorated with gold or silver
Gold leaf was polished with a stone or a tooth
The Book of Kells, about 800, has a famous Chi-Rho page

questions.prompt: What were the finest medieval manuscripts written on?

options.label: Thin sheets of beaten gold
options.rationale: Gold was added as decoration, not used as the page.

options.label: Wooden panels like icons
options.rationale: Icons were painted on wood; books used vellum.

questions.explanation: The finest manuscripts were written on vellum, a parchment made from calfskin.

questions.prompt: Strictly speaking, what makes a manuscript "illuminated"?

options.label: It was written by candlelight
options.rationale: The word refers to the decoration, not how it was written.

options.label: It is decorated with gold or silver
It contains the four Gospels
options.rationale: Plenty of illuminated books aren't Gospels.

options.label: It was copied in a monastery
options.rationale: Many were, but that's not what the word means.

questions.explanation: In the strict sense, only manuscripts decorated with gold or silver, which catch the light, are illuminated.

questions.prompt: The Chi-Rho page turns one holy word into a whole picture. Which art from Level 22 shares that idea?

options.label: Muqarnas ceilings
options.rationale: Those are carved cells, not words.

options.label: Geometric star patterns
options.rationale: Those are pure geometry, not words.

questions.explanation: Both traditions made the holy word itself into art: calligraphy for the Qur'an, the Chi-Rho page for the Gospels.
